name: Massachusetts Backyard 24
blurb: Twenty-four birds you can find from a yard, a sidewalk, or a town park. Start with the eight that come to you, end with two that make a whole spring worth it.
_curation: Chosen for habitat and recognisability, not rarity -- every bird here is
reachable without a scope, a boat, or a 4am drive. Deliberately excluded:
shorebirds, seabirds, marsh specialists and raptors that need open country.
The list runs a seasonal arc on purpose. The easy end is resident feeder
birds you can get in January. The middle brings in a winter visitor (junco,
white-throated sparrow) so the set teaches that some birds only exist here
in the cold. The hard end is spring-and-summer only -- oriole, hummingbird,
grosbeak, tanager -- so a January player physically cannot finish, and has
a reason to still be playing in May.
Cooper's Hawk would belong here but GBIF has no usable Massachusetts
records for it (see fetch_region.py). Left out rather than faked.
